question: Can a fixed Heart representation support card-effect correction when its neural gradient data and readout fitting data are disjoint? Use E185 as a matched representation control for E187.

inputs: Same E185 public normalized state and optional210 E187 derived printed-cost features. No new observations, hidden RNG, seed IDs, future data or labels enter scores. Canonical feature expansion follows the frozen independent E187 dense decoder; neural math is NumPyfloat64 for both arms.
score: P_frozen(s_candidate)-P_frozen(s_parent) plus [h(s_candidate)-h(s_parent)]/fit_only_RMS times64 fitted coefficients. Parent score0. h is the frozen64-dimensional last hidden layer. fit: Weighted ridge against [R_candidate-R_parent]-[P_candidate-P_parent]. Each calibration family has total weight1, divided equally over its menus and nonparent alternatives. Scale each hidden difference by fitting-weighted RMS with floor.01. Solve sum(weight*error^2)+1*sum(beta^2) once; no optimizer or hyperparameter grid. Zero correction is the starting comparison.
controls: Six closed-form fits total:3folds x original/cost representation. Both use identical correction families, menus, targets, numerical precision and regularization. Retain frozen-inner/no-correction and original-parent comparisons.
